conventions.convention: Vertical grid segments pass over horizontal segments; horizontal orientation is O to X and vertical orientation is X to O. Knot inputs have a single cycle in the marking permutation.
A rectangle from x to y has its southwest and northeast corners in x. Empty means its interior contains no source-state point; torus rectangles may wrap across the fundamental-square boundary.
The grid Alexander value is (M_O−M_X)/2−(n−1)/2. Each U_i has Maslov degree −2 and Alexander degree −1.
Tilde counts rectangles avoiding O and X; associated-graded minus avoids X and records O variables; full filtered minus permits X and records O variables.
Balanced knot diagrams have symmetric rank h+k−1, w=O and z=X. Admissibility tests every nonzero periodic domain vanishing at all w marks for both positive and negative coefficients.

Full closed-manifold hat admissibility tests every Spin-c sector, including sectors without generators; it is global weak admissibility. Weak admissibility for one specified sector is a separate condition.
Restriction along U↦U_i retains the other independent variables. Simultaneous ordinary collapse U_1=⋯=U_k=U instead contributes V factors, with V degrees (0,0) and (−1,−1).

Tau is the least integer filtration level whose inclusion has nonzero image in one-dimensional total hat homology. The differential retains positive z multiplicities; its Alexander associated graded is a different complex.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming countable choice, for the stated oriented knot, minimum-genus Seifert surface and compatible diagrams, the chosen-variable grid and analytic complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent with the normalized Alexander filtration. The chosen-variable restriction has type CFK^−(K), whereas ordinary simultaneous collapse has type CFK^−(K)⊗V^(n−1), and tilde homology is hat HFK(K)⊗V^(n−1).

Assuming countable choice, the stated admissible multipointed diagrams for the same oriented knot are related by the specified geometric comparisons, and their full filtered minus complexes restricted to any chosen single variable action are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. Ordinary simultaneous collapse and tilde homology retain the stated V factors.

Assuming countable choice, every admissible balanced multipointed knot diagram in S³ has the stated chosen regular finite disk counts and index-two compactifications, with broken-end gluing and cancellation of boundary-degeneration contributions. Its full disk-count differential squares to zero and preserves Alexander filtration.

Under ACω and the stated operation-specific global weak, ordinary specified-sector weak, or strict admissibility hypotheses, the permitted auxiliary representatives and coherent perturbations give finite zero-dimensional counts and compact one-dimensional polygon and continuation spaces with the stated exhaustive boundaries and count identities. Named top cycles, surgery constructions and move invariance are separate obligations.

For the specified cyclic permutations, commutations and stabilizations, chosen-variable full filtered grid complexes are graded filtered chain homotopy equivalent. Commutation preserves tilde homology; stabilization tensors it with V of degrees (0,0) and (−1,−1).

Non-annular two-rectangle composites have exactly two equal-weight decompositions. Returning thin-annulus terms are excluded or cancel in pairs. Counted terms have Maslov degree −1 and Alexander drop equal to their number of X markings.

The normalized reverse-mirror complex is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the Laurent dual with negated bifiltration coordinates. Separately, the original complex has a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence exchanging its algebraic and Alexander filtrations.

concerns.concern: Verification 1.2 says, “For either ordered pair of distinct states, the rectangles from the first state to the second are the bottom-left and top-right cells,” then assigns the reverse rectangles to the other two cells. The first assertion cannot hold for both ordered pairs: direction determines which diagonal pair occurs. Naming the two states would resolve this wording defect. Both directions remain excluded in tilde mode, so the rank-two conclusion is unaffected.

Proof 2.1 applies the planar disk-slide supplier and says, “Two faces of a repeated other disk are processed separately.” The cited lem-marked-planar-cut-surface-regions-are-realized-by-disk-slides explicitly requires its inner faces to come from distinct disks. The proof should explain the successive one-face planar regions that permit repeated disk labels, rather than apply that supplier directly to the whole cap.

The Statement omits countable choice, while Facts & Assumptions explicitly uses “the ACω disk-count branch stated in the frontmatter,” and its analytic suppliers assume countable choice. State that hypothesis in the uninterrupted Statement so its public scope matches the proof.
